text.p: These are the leading stories in the Lebanese press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Former chief of pro-Iranian Hizbollah movement, Sheikh Tufaili, who is to launch "hunger revolt" campaign of civil disobedience, says: We will not use violence.
- Lebanese treasury bills in Washington to finance electricity projects worth $100 million. Bills are guaranteed by World Bank.
- Details of attack on journalist Pierre Atallah revealed at news conference.
- Prime Minister Hariri back from Morocco.
- Katyusha rockets fall near Israeli borders.
- Government faces hunger revolt with tough security measures.
- Central bank sold Credit Libanais to Saudi group for $163 million.
- Delegation of Iraqi businessmen to visit Lebanon on August 19.
- Israeli helicopters strike in Naameh hills south of Beirut.
